newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek mutual funds grow in 96, assets up 60pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek mutual funds grow in 96, assets up 60pct.

text.p: Greek mutual funds grew to 150 in 1996 from 117 a year earlier while the fund industry's assets under management rose 60 percent to 3.9 trillion drachmas from 2.4 trillion in 1995, the Association of Institutional Investors said on Monday.

Four new fund management companies became members of the Association of Institutional Investors -- ETBA Natwest, Barclays, Hanwha Hellas and General Hellenic Bank, said the association's president Alexios Pilavios during the annual shareholders' meeting.
Its membership numbers 30 fund management companies and 17 closed-end investment funds.

The association will submit proposals for more efficient management of pension fund assets in 1997 and study the impact of Europe's planned common currency, the Euro, on the mutual fund industry, it said.
